problem: Robot datasets limited to a few scenes or tasks do not support open-vocabulary manipulation and cross-lab generalization, and are often evaluated with only one learner.
contribution: BridgeDataV2 combines diverse low-cost-arm demonstrations, scripted pick-and-place trajectories and post-hoc language labels, and evaluates six offline-learning recipes plus size/diversity/model-capacity ablations.
algorithm: The dataset is the contribution rather than a new optimizer. Goal-conditioned BC, diffusion BC, goal-conditioned ACT and contrastive RL use image goals; language BC and RT-1 use language. Collection presents many feasible tasks in each scene, randomizes cameras/objects/workspace every50trajectories and adds imperfect scripted repositioning data.
observations: Stored640x480 camera observations at5Hz; availability of fixed RGB-D, randomized RGB and wrist views varies by episode. Evaluation uses only over-the-shoulder RGB:128x128 for most methods,320x256 for RT-1. Image-goal training samples future observations from the same trajectory.
actions: 7D:6D relative Cartesian end-effector motion plus discrete gripper open/close. These are not SO-101 or ROSMASTER joint-position actions. Teleoperation uses a VR controller.
embodiment_and_data: WidowX250 setup;60,096 trajectories=50,365 human demonstrations+9,731 scripted trajectories,13skill groups,24environments and100+objects. Collection occurred at one institution; another lab provides a zero-shot evaluation with matching hardware.
experiments: Seen-task evaluation, new objects/environments, cross-institution testing, encoder capacity, stratified dataset subsampling and equal-size skill-diversity comparison. Main policy tables use10trials per task; the3-versus13skill ablation uses20trials per policy.
baselines: GCBC,D-GCBC,goal-conditioned ACT,CRL,LCBC,RT-1; BridgeV1+PTR versusV2; ResNet18/34/50 and three-versus13skills. Different image resolutions, histories and action distributions mean these tables are not a clean isolation of architecture alone.

quantitative_result.source: PDF page7 Tables2–3 and page8 Figure5
quantitative_result.conditions: 10trials per task; eight seen and six unseen evaluation tasks. The roughly equal-size3skill versus13skill GCBC comparison reports0.30 versus0.65 on an unseen task with20trials per policy, not general physical success on every skill.

limitations: Mostly low-precision tasks, one collection institution and a single robot morphology; forceful/dynamic/precision-insertion behaviors are underrepresented. Camera/depth coverage is heterogeneous, language can be poorly grounded for unseen objects, and small evaluation denominators limit broad performance claims.

code_and_license.evidence: Paper describes public dataset/pretrained models, but this review does not infer licenses from availability.

hardware_adaptation: ADAPT the episode schema, source labels, scene diversity and balanced skill collection; use selected examples only after rights/schema audit. A WidowX7D Cartesian head cannot be loaded directly into ROSMASTER9D joint/body control. Model and camera resolution should be scaled to measuredNX budgets.
algorithm_detail: AppendixB makes goals future-frame relabels, stacks observation/goal channels and uses standard image augmentations. ACT chunk size is reduced from100 at50Hz to5 at5Hz, so temporal semantics are central. Its reported training uses one2080Ti for3days; this is not a Jetson runtime estimate.
integration_contract: Keep human versus scripted/suboptimal source type, per-episode sensor availability,5Hz timing, task/skill definitions, relative Cartesian frame and gripper convention explicit. Heldout scenes and sessions must remain disjoint; missing camera views must not be synthesized as recorded observations.
license_evidence: No code/data license text was inspected; sourcepaper public-release statements alone do not establish redistribution or checkpoint rights.
required_experiments: Reproduce a compact goal-conditioned baseline with identical action/camera/horizon settings; compare same-size diversity subsets; test cross-session and cross-scene generalization; audit domain shift and rights before any external-data import; independently validate physical outcomes after adaptation.
difference_from_explorer: Broad skill datasets and positive transfer from diverse skills already exist here. Explorer must show explicit retained-skill, diagnosis or cross-embodiment effects beyond counting more episodes or adopting a similar recorder.

evidence_locations.supports: Six learning recipes and trial protocol
